reviewed_surface: migrate reset drops or soft-resets the configured database and reapplies migrations; db push --force-reset resets it before pushing; db push --accept-data-loss applies an unobserved lossy diff; db execute --stdin runs the piped SQL. -h/--help and -v/--version exit without acting.

Built-in Active Record tasks, matched as exact tokens: db:drop, db:reset, db:migrate:reset, db:purge and the test-database purge tasks (db:test:purge, db:test:load_schema, db:test:prepare), with their :all, :NAME and db:drop:_unsafe forms, drop or empty a configured database; db:schema:load and db:setup recreate every table with force: :cascade; db:truncate_all and db:seed:replant truncate every table. db:fixtures:load deletes every row of each table that has a fixture file before inserting the fixtures. Several tasks may be given in one call. Rails commands such as runner, console and generate take no tasks. -v is the version command only as the first argument; after a task it reaches Rake, where it means verbose.

The same built-in Active Record tasks run through rake, matched as exact tokens; NAME=value operands are environment assignments. -T/-D/-W/-P list tasks and -n/--dry-run skips actions; rake -e (inline Ruby) and other options stay unmodeled.
flush removes all data from every table of the selected database; django-extensions reset_db drops and recreates the database. Other commands stay unmodeled.
db:drop drops the configured database. Undo migrations and other commands stay unmodeled.
schema:drop drops every table of the data source's database. schema:sync, schema:log and migrations stay unmodeled.
push applies the schema diff to the configured database; drop removes a migration file, not data, and stays unmodeled.
clean drops every object in the configured schemas. A literal -cleanDisabled=true refuses it; configuration can also disable clean (the default since Flyway 9), which Nah does not read.
drop-all drops every database object in the configured schemas; --force and --require-force take picocli boolean values. Rollback commands stay unmodeled.
drop drops the target database. Global options precede the command; rollback stays unmodeled.

Two tools share the atlas name with disjoint subcommands: Ariga's schema clean drops every object in the target database; the MongoDB Atlas CLI's clusters (alias cluster) delete (alias rm) and serverless delete remove the deployment and its backup snapshots.

projects (alias project), branches (alias branch) and databases (aliases database, db) delete remove the named resource; branches reset --parent and branches restore overwrite a branch's data, optionally preserving the old state under a new name. -h/--help and -v/--version exit without acting. Endpoint (compute) deletion stays unmodeled.

database (alias db) delete (alias rm) removes a database and branch delete (alias rm) removes a branch (and with --delete-descendants its descendants). Password, role and backup commands stay unmodeled.

db destroy removes each named database (one or more); with a nonempty --location or --instance it removes only one replica or instance instead. group destroy removes a group and all of its databases; db shell runs SQL against the named database.

d1 delete removes a D1 database. d1 execute --remote runs --command SQL once against the Cloudflare database, or its preview database with --preview. Without --remote it targets the local Miniflare state on disk; Wrangler refuses --preview without --remote, --local with --remote, and a nonempty --persist-to without --local.

pg:reset deletes all data in the database (DATABASE_URL by default); pg:backups:restore and pg:copy replace the target database's contents. The attachment names do not identify the database, so the target stays unresolved.

redis delete, vector delete and search delete remove the database or index named by id (--dry-run only prints); redis exec FLUSHALL or FLUSHDB empties the database. Other exec commands stay unmodeled.

db reset --linked or --db-url drops the remote database's user schemas and reapplies migrations and seeds; the default local reset targets the development container. projects delete and branches delete remove the named project or branch, or one chosen at a prompt when no target is given.

databases delete (alias rm; databases also answers to database, db, dbs and d) removes a managed database cluster; databases db delete removes one database from a cluster. -h/--help exits without acting, for these and for compute droplet delete.

mix ecto.drop drops the storage of each configured repo. ecto.reset is a project alias defined in mix.exs, not an Ecto task, and stays unmodeled. ecto.reset is not an Ecto task but the alias Phoenix generates in mix.exs as ecto.drop followed by ecto.setup; mix.exs is not read, so it is taken to drop the database.
bundle exec runs the given command inside the bundle after evaluating the Gemfile.

db:wipe drops every table (and with --drop-views/--drop-types views and types); migrate:fresh runs db:wipe then migrate; migrate:reset runs every migration's down method, unless --pretend only prints the SQL; migrate:refresh resets every migration unless --step is a positive number, which rolls back that many instead. In production each asks for confirmation unless --force. migrate:rollback and other commands stay unmodeled. A command name whose colon segments each prefix a modeled command's (migrate:fr) is read as that command, as Symfony Console resolves it against the registered commands. --database, --path, --schema-path, --seeder, --step and --env take optional values. -h/--help and -V/--version exit without acting.

doctrine:database:drop drops the connection's database only with -f/--force and otherwise prints what it would drop; doctrine:schema:drop drops the mapped schema (or with --full-database every asset) only with -f/--force, and --dump-sql prints the SQL instead; doctrine:fixtures:load purges every mapped table with DELETE (or TRUNCATE with --purge-with-truncate) unless --append or --dry-run, asking for confirmation only when interactive. Other commands stay unmodeled; a command name whose colon segments each prefix a modeled command's (d:d:d) is read as that command, as Symfony Console resolves it. -h/--help and -V/--version exit without acting.
